name: RPX
description: RPX (Robot Perception X) is a real-world benchmark for evaluating robot perception as manipulation changes a scene. It captures 100 scenes (50 indoor, 50 outdoor, at 20 sites) in three exocentric phases, before (Clutter), during (Interaction) and after (Clean) manipulation, plus an egocentric view during Interaction, and scans 70 everyday objects alone in 360 degrees: about 133,000 frames in total (75,000 multi-object, 23,121 egocentric, 35,000 single-object). Annotations include instance masks, tracklets, metric depth, 6-DoF camera pose, object questionnaires and VQA questions. Six tasks are scored on the same scenes: image depth, video depth, multi-object tracking, relative camera pose, VQA localization and in-context VQA.
citeAs: @misc{rpx2026, title={Same Scene, Different Story: Evaluating Robot Perception Across Scene Phases in the Wild}, author={{Jishnu Jaykumar P} and Kadosh, Itay and Vijayakumar, Narendhiran and Kamath, Srinanditha and Allu, Sai Haneesh and Rangappa, Govind Tyagi and Maheshwari, Animesh and Wang, Jikai and Xiang, Yu}, year={2026}, note={Dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/IRVLUTD/RPX}}

creator.name: Intelligent Robotics and Vision Lab, The University of Texas at Dallas

dataCollection: Data was collected with a hand-held sensor rig (Intel RealSense D435 RGB-D and T265 fisheye stereo with visual-inertial pose) operated by lab members, plus a head-mounted GoPro during Interaction. Each of 100 scenes was captured in three phases: Clutter, Interaction and Clean. Instance masks were generated with SAM2 propagation and iterative human correction. Camera poses come from T265 visual-inertial odometry. Object attributes come from per-object questionnaires.
dataBiases: Scenes come from 20 capture sites (10 indoor, 10 outdoor) and arrange 6-8 of 70 everyday household and workplace objects on surfaces such as tables, benches and steps. Depth is limited to the D435 sensing range; trajectories are hand-held rather than robot-mounted; capture and annotation were done by lab personnel, so annotator diversity is limited.
personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains video footage of human hands during the interaction phase. No faces, biometric identifiers, or personally identifiable information are captured or released. Participants provided informed consent for data collection and release.
